evals.name: job-lease-stale-worker
evals.prompt: Can you prove our job queue never lets a job's result get clobbered or processed twice? Lease logic is in src/store.ts and src/worker.ts. I want an actual proof or a concrete counterexample, not more unit tests.
evals.expected_output: Models lease expiry as an environment action, finds that a stale worker (lease expired, job reclaimed) still calls complete() and overwrites the result, and that side effects run twice. Explains that leases give at-least-once processing so exactly-once side effects are impossible without idempotency. Proposes fencing token / owner check on complete (UPDATE ... WHERE owner=$ AND token=$). Re-verifies the fix; HTML report.

evals.name: rust-pool-capacity-and-hang
evals.prompt: Our connection pool in src/lib.rs sometimes goes over max connections under load, and every so often a request thread hangs forever in acquire(). Can you model it formally, find out why, and fix it?
evals.expected_output: Finds (1) check-then-act on in_use across two separate lock acquisitions -> more than max checked out (safety, invariant violation), and (2) lost wakeup: acquire checks then re-locks and waits (notification can land between), and release notifies before decrementing -> waiter sleeps forever (deadlock/liveness). Fix: one mutex guarding the count (and idle list), check-and-increment under one guard, while-loop condvar wait on that same guard, decrement then notify. Re-verifies safety and deadlock-freedom/liveness; adds a Rust regression test (threads + barriers, or loom/shuttle if available); cargo test passes; HTML report.
assertions: Identifies the capacity race: in_use is checked and incremented under two separate lock acquisitions, so more than max connections can be checked out
Identifies the lost-wakeup/hang: the waiter re-locks and waits after checking (notification can land in between) and/or release notifies before decrementing
A model checker or prover was run and produced counterexamples for both the capacity violation (safety) and the hang (deadlock or liveness)
